answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring cryptographic proof of staked computational resource scarcity, anchoring network privileges to a scarce physical relic rather than infinitely reproducible software instances. If an adversary attempts to spawn fake identities, the protocol forces them to lock up verifiable physical assets or expend measurable energy akin to mining copper, driving the marginal cost of creating a new agent past the economic tipping point of the ledger, thereby rendering unauthorized identity inflation unprofitable.
